Looking at this problem, I need to find the cardinality of the set of isomorphism classes of binary relations on ℕ, where two relations are equivalent iff one can be transformed into the other by a bijection (permutation) of ℕ.

**Interpretation.** Each $r \subseteq \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ is a directed graph on vertex set $\mathbb{N}$. The relation $R$ identifies two directed graphs when they are isomorphic (via a bijection $\pi: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$). So $P(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})/{_R}$ is the set of isomorphism classes of countable directed graphs.

**Verification that $R$ is an equivalence relation.** Reflexive: take $\pi = \mathrm{id}$. Symmetric: if $\pi$ sends $r$ to $s$, then $\pi^{-1}$ sends $s$ to $r$. Transitive: if $\pi$ sends $r$ to $s$ and $\sigma$ sends $s$ to $t$, then $\sigma\circ\pi$ sends $r$ to $t$. ✓

---

### Upper bound: $|P(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})/{_R}| \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$

The number of equivalence classes cannot exceed the size of the underlying set:
$$|P(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})/{_R}| \leq |P(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})| = 2^{|\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}|} = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

---

### Lower bound: $|P(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})/{_R}| \geq 2^{\aleph_0}$

I construct an injection $\Phi: P(\mathbb{N}) \to P(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})/{_R}$, assigning to each subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ a distinct isomorphism class.

**Construction.** For each $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, define a directed graph $G_S$ on vertex set $\mathbb{N}$ as a disjoint union of directed cycles, one for each $n \geq 1$:
- If $n \in S$: the $n$-th component is a directed cycle of length $2n+1$ (odd).
- If $n \notin S$: the $n$-th component is a directed cycle of length $2n$ (even).

Since the total number of vertices is $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} c_n$ where each $c_n \in \{2n,\, 2n+1\}$, this is a countably infinite sum of positive integers, hence countable. We can biject these vertices with $\mathbb{N}$, realizing $G_S$ as a relation $r_S \subseteq \mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$.

**Key observation.** The set of cycle lengths appearing in $G_S$ is:
$$L_S = \{c_n : n \geq 1\}, \quad c_n = \begin{cases} 2n+1 & \text{if } n \in S,\\ 2n & \text{if } n \notin S.\end{cases}$$

For each $n \geq 1$, exactly one of $\{2n,\, 2n+1\}$ belongs to $L_S$. No cycle length is repeated (each integer $\geq 2$ arises from at most one index $n$). Therefore $L_S$ is a **set** (not a multiset with repetitions), and it uniquely determines $S$:
$$n \in S \iff 2n+1 \in L_S \iff 2n \notin L_S.$$

**Injectivity.** The isomorphism type of a disjoint union of directed cycles is completely determined by the multiset of cycle lengths. Since in our construction there are no repeated lengths, this multiset is the set $L_S$. If $S \neq S'$, there exists $n \in S \triangle S'$; say $n \in S \setminus S'$. Then $2n+1 \in L_S \setminus L_{S'}$ and $2n \in L_{S'} \setminus L_S$, so $L_S \neq L_{S'}$, hence $G_S \not\cong G_{S'}$, i.e., $[r_S] \neq [r_{S'}]$ in $P(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})/{_R}$.

Therefore $\Phi$ is injective, giving:
$$|P(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})/{_R}| \geq |P(\mathbb{N})| = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

---

### Conclusion

Combining both bounds:
$$|P(\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N})/{_R}| = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

The cardinality of the set of equivalence classes is $\boxed{2^{\aleph_0}}$ (the cardinality of the continuum).
